title: Belt and Road sample: capability and accuracy tests (4 real events)
method: For each event the platform's evidence-pack script searched public sources automatically and was compared item by item with authoritative facts in bri/reference.json. The 2026-08-26 event was detected live by the platform; the other 3 are back-tests where the seed was only the first public report available at the time (time, place, link) and the script found the rest. All times UTC.

tests.name: Kerung–Rasuwa flood (Nepal, 2026-08-26)
tests.mode: Live: detected automatically by the platform
tests.nearest_project: Kerung–Kathmandu railway (planned) 6.7 km; Syaphrubesi–Rasuwagadhi highway 14 km; Rasuwagadhi border post 15 km (distance to the reference source area)
rows: Yes (GDACS red alert created the event automatically)
1 h 52 min early: the GDACS time is not the actual onset
USGS M5.2, EMSC ms5.2, IO.EVN, KKN and citizen seismometers all at 02:52–02:53
Not judged (only relayed: USGS classed it as 'collapse/landslide, non-tectonic')
Ice-rock avalanche turning into a debris flow; not a glacial lake, rain or earthquake
Relayed USGS class matches the reference
Used the GDACS point, south of Kathmandu
Off by 108 km; nearby river gauges were listed for the Bagmati basin and the Trishuli gauges were missed
Reference sources contradict each other (157 dead / over 390 dead or missing / over 1,400 missing)
Sentinel-2 next day (54% cloud); Sentinel-1 and Copernicus automatic flood extent after 2.4 days
Wikipedia article created 3 hours later; Copernicus EMS mapping EMSR927 activated after 7 hours
About 1 hour before the collapse, citizen seismometer AM.R02C2 showed a signal 395× background; IO.EVN also had a signal the day before
ICIMOD notes analyses saying it was visible on the afternoon of the 25th
Platform records only, does not interpret

tests.name: Rasuwagadhi glacial lake outburst flood (Nepal, 2025-07-08)
tests.mode: Back-test: seed was an All India Radio report at 06:44
tests.nearest_project: Syaphrubesi–Rasuwagadhi highway and Kerung–Kathmandu railway 0.1 km; Rasuwagadhi border post 2.8 km
rows: GDELT found one at 03:45 (09:30 local), 3 hours before the seed
Correct; within a few hours of onset
No clear signal during the flood (KKN only a few single-station signals, timing does not match)
Eos cites a station near Kathmandu recording a signal about 1 hour before the flood reached the border
Missed: our '1–5 Hz, 60 s, 5× background' method is insensitive to sustained flood vibration
The glacial lake outburst database lists this outburst (in China, 30 km from the border post)
Supraglacial lake outburst on Purepu glacier, Tibet
About 30 dead or missing (ICIMOD); 9 bodies and 19 missing (All India Radio); 11 dead (Himal Press)
Right magnitude, different definitions (dead vs dead plus missing)
Sentinel-1 after 1.5 days with Copernicus automatic flood extent; Sentinel-2 cloudy until 19 August
Radar available, optical limited by cloud
Friendship Bridge washed away; 4 hydropower plants damaged; hundreds of vehicles destroyed
Missing: the platform does not extract damage from news
Wikipedia matched a 2026 article; river gauges showed the state two years later

tests.name: Karakoram Highway washed out at Mor (Pakistan, 2025-08-08)
tests.mode: Back-test: seed was a ProPakistani report the next day
rows: GDELT found Daily Times at 13:30 the same day: 'Flood cuts off China–Pakistan road'
Sentinel-2 next day 05:37 (18% cloud), road section directly visible; Sentinel-1 after 2 days
IODA shows no clear national drop in Pakistan
Only national level visible, not Gilgit-Baltistan
IODA region name did not match
The old scan only covered the central Himalaya; the new project scan searches news for 'Karakoram Highway' and would likely catch it

tests.name: Landslide in Na district, Oudomxay, 9 missing (Laos, 2025-04-29)
tests.mode: Back-test: seed was a Lao News Agency report
tests.nearest_project: China–Laos Railway 6.3 km (district town known, village location unknown)
rows: Only the seed itself (about 12 hours after); none in GDELT English news
New Sentinel-1 scene 17 hours after; Sentinel-2 after 6 days (50% cloud)
Uncertain, possibly off by a few to over ten km
The new project scan searches news for 'China–Laos Railway'; this event was unrelated to the railway and would be missed
Missed: needs local Lao news and district-level place names

overall: Events seismometers can 'hear' (ice-rock avalanches, large landslides): onset time within 1 minute, and a second collapse can be separated.
Floods and ordinary landslides: mainly from news; the platform lags hours to half a day; English news barely covers countries like Laos.
Location: GDACS points can be off by more than 100 km; place names in news get to village or district level.

Casualties and damage: largely not obtained (only in databases such as the GLOF database and Nepal's disaster authority). Filling this needs ReliefWeb (pending an approved appname) and national disaster databases.
Satellite: a new radar scene always within 0.5–2.5 days; optical depends on cloud, from the next day to weeks.
Testing found 4 bugs in the evidence-pack script; all fixed and re-run.
not_covered: Conflict and security events (such as attacks in Gwadar) were not tested: there is no authoritative item-by-item reference, so accuracy is hard to quantify.
Only 4 events: conclusions are indicative, not a statistical accuracy rate.
